\label{lemma-proper-flat-noetherian}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a perfect proper morphism of Noetherian schemes.
Let $a$ be the right adjoint for
$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ of
Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image}. Then $a$ commutes with direct sums.

final_content.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. For every family $(K_\lambda)$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the canonical comparison $\bigoplus_\lambda a_f(K_\lambda)\to a_f(\bigoplus_\lambda K_\lambda)$ is an isomorphism. This does not require $f$ to be flat; perfectness and properness are the relevant assumptions.
hypotheses: f perfect proper between Noetherian schemes.
conclusions: The right adjoint of Rf_* preserves direct sums.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-flat-noetherian-relative}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a perfect proper morphism of Noetherian schemes.
Let $a$ be the right adjoint for
$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ of
Lemma \ref{lemma-twisted-inverse-image}. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every closed $T \subset Y$ if $Q \in D_\QCoh(Y)$ is supported on $T$,
then $a(Q)$ is supported on $f^{-1}(T)$,
\item for every open $V \subset Y$ and any $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
the map (\ref{equation-sheafy}) is an isomorphism, and
\end{enumerate}

final_content.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. A complex in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ is *supported on* a closed subset $T$ if every cohomology sheaf is zero on $Y\setminus T$. If $V\subseteq Y$ is open, $U=f^{-1}(V)$, and $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $j':U\hookrightarrow X$, the *restriction comparison* is the natural map $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_{f|_U}(j^*K)$. Then (1) for every closed $T\subseteq Y$, any $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ supported on $T$ has $a_f(Q)$ supported on $f^{-1}(T)$; and (2) for every open $V\subseteq Y$ and every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the natural restriction map $\rho_K:a_f(K)|_{f^{-1}(V)}\to a_{f|_{f^{-1}(V)}}(K|_V)$ is an isomorphism, understood locally on the open $V$ when it is not quasi-compact.
hypotheses: f perfect proper Noetherian; T closed and V open.
conclusions: a_f preserves supports and localizes on arbitrary opens.

final_content.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. For every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, including unbounded $K$, the canonical projection-comparison morphism
\[
Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_f(K)
\]
is an isomorphism. This requires perfect properness, but not flatness.
hypotheses: f perfect proper Noetherian, a_f right adjoint.
conclusions: The projection formula for the right adjoint holds on all unbounded quasi-coherent-derived inputs.

The final preserves that, does not silently substitute flat properness or require K perfect.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-proper-perfect-base-change}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a perfect proper morphism of Noetherian schemes.
Let $g : Y' \to Y$ be a morphism with $Y'$ Noetherian. If $X$ and
$Y'$ are tor independent over $Y$, then the base
change map (\ref{equation-base-change-map}) is an isomorphism
for all $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.

final_content.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism with $Y'$ Noetherian, form $X'=X\times_YY'$ with $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, and assume $X$ and $Y'$ are Tor-independent over $Y$. Then the canonical right-adjoint base-change transformation
\[
L(g')^*a_f(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_{f'}(Lg^*K)
\]
is an isomorphism for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, where the map is the mate of the usual Tor-independent derived pushforward base change. Tor-independence cannot be omitted merely because the morphisms are perfect.
hypotheses: f perfect proper Noetherian, Y' Noetherian, Tor-independent cartesian square.
conclusions: Duality base change is an isomorphism under Tor-independence.

semantic_review_note: Pinned duality.tex L3114 requires perfect proper f between Noetherian schemes, Y' NOETHERIAN, and X and Y' TOR-INDEPENDENT over Y. It concludes the base-change mate L(g')^*a_f(K)→a_{f'}(Lg^*K) is an isomorphism on ALL D_QCoh(Y). The proposed condition retains Tor-independence explicitly despite f being perfect.
